sentences.zh: 姚泓

translations.literal: Section heading: Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: 姚泓，字元子，興之長子也。

translations.literal: Yao Hong, courtesy name Yuanzi, was the eldest son of Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong, courtesy Yuanzi, was Yao Xing's firstborn.

sentences.zh: 孝友寬和，而無經世之用，又多疾病，興將以為嗣而疑焉。

translations.literal: He was filial, friendly, generous, and mild, yet lacked the ability to order the age, and moreover often fell ill; Xing was about to make him heir yet hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: He was dutiful, gentle, and kind, but had no talent for governing a realm, and he was often ill—so Yao Xing long hesitated before naming him heir.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃立為太子。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was then established as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At length Yao Xing named him crown prince.

sentences.zh: 興每征伐巡遊，常留總後事。

translations.literal: Whenever Xing on campaign or inspection tour, he regularly left him behind to oversee rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yao Xing marched or toured, he left Yao Hong in charge of the rear.

sentences.zh: 博學善談論，尤好詩詠。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and good at discourse, especially fond of poetry and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned, a fluent talker, and especially loved poetry.

sentences.zh: 尚書王尚、黃門郎段章、尚書郎富允文以儒術侍講，胡義周、夏侯稚以文章遊集。

translations.literal: Director Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Duan Zhang, and Director Gentleman Fu Yunwen attended lectures with Confucian learning; Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi gathered in literary companionship.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang, Duan Zhang, and Fu Yunwen tutored him in the classics; Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi kept him company over belles-lettres.

sentences.zh: 時尚書王敏、右丞郭播以刑政過寬，議欲峻制，泓曰：「人情挫辱，則壯厲之心生；

translations.literal: At the time Director Wang Min and right aide Guo Bo, because punishments and government were too lenient, debated wishing for harsh regulation. Hong said, "When human feelings are humiliated, a fierce and stern mind arises;
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang Min and aide Guo Bo thought the laws too soft and pressed for crackdowns. Yao Hong replied: "Humiliate people and you breed defiance.

sentences.zh: 政教煩苛，則苟免之行立。

translations.literal: When government and instruction are fussy and harsh, conduct of bare escape is established.
translations.idiomatic: Smother them in petty rules and they learn only to dodge.

sentences.zh: 上之化下，如風靡草。

translations.literal: What is above transforms what is below, like wind bending grass.
translations.idiomatic: Those above shape those below as wind bends grass.

sentences.zh: 君等參贊朝化，弘昭政軌，不務仁恕之道，惟欲嚴法酷刑，豈是安上馭下之理乎！

translations.literal: You gentlemen assist and join in court transformation, broadly display the tracks of government—if you do not pursue the way of benevolence and forgiveness, but only desire harsh laws and cruel punishments, how could that be the principle of quieting those above and controlling those below!"
translations.idiomatic: You help run the court—widen the path of mercy, not the jailer's whip; harshness is no way to steady ruler and people."

sentences.zh: 」敏等遂止。

translations.literal: Min and others then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Min and his allies dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 泓受經于博士淳于岐。

translations.literal: Hong received the classics from Erudite Chunyu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong studied the classics under the erudite Chunyu Qi.

sentences.zh: 岐病，泓親詣省疾，拜於床下。

translations.literal: When Qi was ill, Hong personally went to inquire after his illness and bowed below the couch.
translations.idiomatic: When Chunyu Qi fell ill, Yao Hong visited his bedside and bowed on the floor.

sentences.zh: 自是公侯見師傅皆拜焉。

translations.literal: From this dukes and marquises seeing tutors all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: After that, every prince who met a tutor bowed as he had done.

sentences.zh: 興之如平涼也，馮翊人劉厥聚眾數千，據萬年以叛。

translations.literal: When Xing went to Pingliang, a man of Fengyi, Liu Jue, gathered several thousand followers, occupied Wannian, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing marched to Pingliang, Liu Jue of Fengyi raised several thousand men, seized Wannian, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 泓遣鎮軍彭白狼率東宮禁兵討之，斬厥，赦其餘黨。

translations.literal: Hong sent General Who Guards the Army Peng Bailang to lead eastern-palace household troops to campaign against him, beheaded Jue, and pardoned the rest of the faction.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Peng Bailang with palace guards from the heir's residence; Liu Jue was executed and the rest pardoned.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸勸泓曰：「殿下神算電發，蕩平醜逆，宜露布表言，廣其首級，以慰遠近之情。

translations.literal: The generals all urged Hong, saying, "Your Highness's divine calculations strike like lightning; you have swept away the vile rebels—it is fitting to issue a public bulletin reporting it, broadly display their heads, to comfort feeling far and near."
translations.idiomatic: His generals said: "Your victory was swift—publish a victory notice and show the heads to steady the realm."

sentences.zh: 」泓曰：「主上委吾後事，使式遏寇逆。

translations.literal: Hong said, "The lord above entrusted me with rear affairs, making me check invading rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong answered: "My father left me the rear to stop traitors.

sentences.zh: 吾綏禦失和，以長奸寇，方當引咎責躬，歸罪行間，安敢過自矜誕，以重罪責乎！

translations.literal: I failed in pacification and control, thereby growing traitorous bandits; I ought to take blame on myself and assign guilt among the ranks—how dare I overmuch boast and swagger, thereby adding to the burden of fault!"
translations.idiomatic: I mishandled the pacification and fed rebellion—I should blame myself, not strut and deepen my fault."

sentences.zh: 」其右僕射韋華聞而謂河南太守慕容築曰：「皇太子實有恭惠之德，社稷之福也。

translations.literal: His right vice-director Wei Hua heard it and said to Henan Grand Administrator Murong Zhu, "The crown prince truly has the virtue of reverence and kindness—blessing for the altars."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hua told Murong Zhu: "The crown prince's humility is the dynasty's luck."

sentences.zh: 」其弟弼有奪嫡之謀，泓恩撫如初，未嘗見於色。

translations.literal: His younger brother Bi had a plan to seize the heirship; Hong treated him with favor as at first and never showed it in his expression.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yao Bi plotted to supplant him, yet Yao Hong treated him with unchanged kindness and never showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 姚紹每為弼羽翼，泓亦推心宗事，弗以為嫌。

translations.literal: Yao Shao often acted as wings for Bi; Hong also gave him whole-hearted clan duty and did not take it as suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao backed Yao Bi, but Yao Hong still trusted him as kin and showed no distrust.

sentences.zh: 及僭立，任紹以兵權，紹亦感而歸誠，卒守其忠烈。

translations.literal: When he presumptuously mounted the throne, he entrusted Shao with military authority; Shao was also moved and returned sincerity, and in the end kept his loyal fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yao Hong took the throne he gave Yao Shao real command; Shao repaid him with loyalty unto death.

sentences.zh: 其明識寬裕，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His clear insight and generous breadth were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His judgment and magnanimity ran in that vein throughout.

sentences.zh: 興既死，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: After Xing died, they secretly did not issue mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing died, the court hid the news.

sentences.zh: 南陽公姚愔及大將軍尹元等謀為亂，泓皆誅之。

translations.literal: Duke of Nanyang Yao Yin and Grand General Yin Yuan and others plotted rebellion; Hong executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yin, Yin Yuan, and their fellow plotters were put to death.

sentences.zh: 命其齊公姚恢殺安定太守呂超，恢久乃誅之。

translations.literal: He ordered Duke of Qi Yao Hui to kill Anding Grand Administrator Lü Chao; Hui long delayed before killing him.
translations.idiomatic: He told Duke Qi Yao Hui to kill Lü Chao, governor of Anding; Yao Hui dragged his feet before obeying.

sentences.zh: 泓疑恢有陰謀，恢自是懷貳，陰聚兵甲焉。

translations.literal: Hong suspected Hui had a hidden plot; Hui from this harbored two minds and secretly gathered armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong suspected treason; Yao Hui began to hedge and stockpile arms in secret.

sentences.zh: 泓發喪，以僭即帝位，大赦殊死已下，改元永和，廬於諮議堂。

translations.literal: Hong issued mourning, presumptuously assumed the imperial seat, greatly pardoned all short of capital crime, changed the era to Yonghe, and lodged in a mourning hut at the consultation hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong announced the death, claimed the throne, declared a general amnesty short of capital crimes, adopted the era Yonghe, and mourned in a hut beside the council hall.

sentences.zh: 既葬，乃親庶政，內外百僚增位一等，令文武各盡直言，政有不便於時，事有光益宗廟者，極言勿有所諱。

translations.literal: After burial, he then personally attended to myriad government; inner and outer hundred officials were raised one rank in position; he ordered civil and military each to exhaust straight speech—where government had what was not convenient to the time, or affairs that could add lustre to the ancestral temple, speak to the utmost without hiding.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral he took the reins himself, promoted every official a grade, and invited blunt counsel on what helped or hurt the state.

sentences.zh: 初，興徙李閏羌三千家于安定，尋徙新支。

translations.literal: At first, Xing had moved three thousand households of Li-run Qiang to Anding, then soon moved them to Xin-zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing had earlier moved three thousand Li-run Qiang households to Anding, then shifted them again to Xin-zhi.

sentences.zh: 至是，羌酋党容率所部叛還，遣撫軍姚贊討之。

translations.literal: At this point, Qiang chief Dang Rong led his following in revolt to return; he sent General Who Pacifies Yao Zan to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Their chief Dang Rong then bolted for home; Yao Hong sent Yao Zan against him.

sentences.zh: 容降，徙其豪右數百戶于長安，余遣還李閏。

translations.literal: Rong surrendered; he moved several hundred notable households to Chang'an and sent the rest back to Li-run.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Rong yielded; Yao Hong moved the head families to Chang'an and let the rest go home to Li-run.

sentences.zh: 北地太守毛雍據趙氏塢以叛于泓，姚紹討擒之。

translations.literal: Beidi Grand Administrator Mao Yong occupied the Zhao clan stockade and rebelled against Hong; Yao Shao campaigned, seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yong of Beidi seized the Zhao stockade in revolt; Yao Shao captured him.

sentences.zh: 姚宣時鎮李閏，未知雍敗，遣部將姚佛生等來衛長安。

translations.literal: Yao Xuan then garrisoned Li-run, not yet knowing of Yong's defeat, sent subordinate generals Yao Fosheng and others to come guard Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xuan still held Li-run and, unaware of Mao Yong's fall, sent Yao Fosheng toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 眾既發，宣參軍韋宗奸諂好亂，說宣曰：「主上初立，威化末著，勃勃強盛，侵害必深，本朝之難未可弭也。

translations.literal: Once the host had set out, Xuan's adviser Wei Zong, fawning and fond of turmoil, spoke to Xuan, saying, "The lord has just risen, awe and transformation are not yet manifest; Bobo is strong and flourishing, harm and invasion will surely be deep; the hardship of this court is not yet to be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Adviser Wei Zong, a troublemaker, told Yao Xuan: "The new ruler lacks prestige; Helian Bobo is too strong—the capital's troubles are not over."

sentences.zh: 殿下居維城之任，宜深慮之。

translations.literal: Your Highness holds the duty of the bulwark city—you ought deeply to ponder it.
translations.idiomatic: You hold the western shield—think hard."

sentences.zh: 邢望地形險固，總三方之要，若能據之，虛心撫禦，非但克固維城，亦霸王之業也。

translations.literal: Xingwang's terrain is perilous and firm, gathering the key of three directions—if you can occupy it, with empty mind soothe and control, not only can you solidify the bulwark, it is also the enterprise of a hegemon-king."
translations.idiomatic: Xingwang is a natural fortress commanding three approaches—seize it in earnest and you secure the west and maybe build a power base."

sentences.zh: 」宣乃率戶三萬八千，棄李閏，南保邢望。

translations.literal: Xuan then led thirty-eight thousand households, abandoned Li-run, and went south to hold Xingwang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xuan marched thirty-eight thousand households south from Li-run to fortify Xingwang.

sentences.zh: 宣既南移，諸羌據李閏以叛，紹進討破之。

translations.literal: Once Xuan had moved south, the various Qiang occupied Li-run in revolt; Shao advanced and campaigned, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xuan left, the Qiang seized Li-run; Yao Shao smashed them.

sentences.zh: 宣詣紹歸罪，紹怒殺之。

translations.literal: Xuan went to Shao to confess guilt; Shao in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xuan surrendered to Yao Shao, who killed him in fury.

sentences.zh: 初，宣在邢望，泓遣姚佛生諭宣，佛生遂贊成宣計。

translations.literal: At first, while Xuan was at Xingwang, Hong sent Yao Fosheng to instruct Xuan; Fosheng then endorsed Xuan's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to recall Yao Xuan; Fosheng instead backed the defection.

sentences.zh: 紹數其罪，又戮之。

translations.literal: Shao enumerated his crimes and executed him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao listed Fosheng's crimes and put him to death too.

sentences.zh: 泓下書，士卒死王事，贈以爵位，永復其家。

translations.literal: Hong issued a document: soldiers who died in the king's service were granted rank and title, and their families were forever exempted.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed pensions and perpetual exemptions for families of soldiers who died in royal service.

sentences.zh: 將封宮臣十六人五等子男，姚贊諫曰：「東宮文武，自當有守忠之誠，未有赫然之效，何受封之多乎？

translations.literal: He was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as fifth-rank barons and viscounts; Yao Zan remonstrated, saying, "Eastern-palace civil and military naturally ought to have the loyalty of guarding unto death—they have not yet had blazing manifest merit; how can they receive so many enfeoffments?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan objected to raising sixteen household officers to noble rank: "The heir's staff owes loyalty by duty—they have done nothing spectacular yet."

sentences.zh: 」泓曰：「懸爵於朝，所以懲勸來效，標明盛德。

translations.literal: Hong said, "Suspending rank in court is to punish and encourage coming merit and mark splendid virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong replied: "Titles exist to reward future service and mark true virtue.

sentences.zh: 元子遭家不造，與宮臣同此百憂，獨享其福，得不愧於心乎！

translations.literal: Yuanzi meets the house in misfortune, sharing every worry with palace officials—how could he alone enjoy the blessing without shame in heart!"
translations.idiomatic: I share every grief with my household staff—how could I hoard favors for myself alone?"

sentences.zh: 」贊默然。

translations.literal: Zan was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 姚紹進曰：「陛下不忘報德，封之是也，古者敬其事，命之以始，可須來春，然後議之。

translations.literal: Yao Shao advanced and said, "Your Majesty not forgetting to repay virtue—enfeoffing them is right; the ancients respected the affair and charged them with its beginning—it is possible to wait until next spring, then deliberate."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao urged delay: "Reward them, yes, but wait until spring as the ancients would."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 并州、定陽、貳城胡數萬落叛泓，入於平陽，攻立義姚成都於匈奴堡，推匈奴曹弘為大單于，所在殘掠。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of settlements of Hu in Bingzhou, Dingyang, and Ercheng rebelled against Hong and entered Pingyang, attacked and set up Yao Chengdu of Liyi at the Xiongnu fort, pushed Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Hu households in Bing, Dingyang, and Ercheng rose, poured into Pingyang, crowned Cao Hong shanyu, and pillaged widely.

sentences.zh: 征東姚懿自蒲阪討弘，戰於平陽，大破之，執弘，送于長安，徙其豪右萬五千落於雍州。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi from Puban campaigned against Hong, fought at Pingyang, greatly defeated him, seized Hong, sent him to Chang'an, and moved fifteen thousand notable settlements to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi marched from Puban, shattered them at Pingyang, sent Cao Hong to Chang'an, and resettled fifteen thousand elite households in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 仇池公楊盛攻陷祁山，執建節王總，遂逼秦州。

translations.literal: Duke of Chouqi Yang Sheng attacked and took Qishan, seized Jianjie Wang Zong, then pressed Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng of Chouqi seized Qishan, captured Wang Zong, and drove on Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 泓遣後將軍姚平救之，盛引退。

translations.literal: Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to rescue him; Sheng withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Yao Ping; Yang Sheng pulled back.

sentences.zh: 姚嵩與平追盛及於竹嶺，姚贊率隴西太守姚秦都、略陽太守王煥以禁兵赴之。

translations.literal: Yao Song with Ping pursued Sheng as far as Bamboo Ridge; Yao Zan led Longxi Grand Administrator Yao Qindu and Lüeyang Grand Administrator Wang Huan with household troops to hurry there.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Song and Yao Ping chased Yang Sheng to Bamboo Ridge while Yao Zan brought Yao Qindu and Wang Huan with palace troops.

sentences.zh: 贊至清水，嵩為盛所敗，嵩及秦都、王煥皆戰死。

translations.literal: When Zan reached Qingshui, Song was defeated by Sheng; Song and Qindu and Wang Huan all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingshui, Yao Zan learned Yao Song had been crushed—Song, Qindu, and Wang Huan all lay dead.

sentences.zh: 贊至秦州，退還仇池。

translations.literal: Zan reached Qinzhou and withdrew to Chouqi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan retreated to Chouqi.

sentences.zh: 先是，天水冀縣石鼓鳴，聲聞數百里，野雉皆雊。

translations.literal: Before this, in Tianshui Jixian a stone drum sounded, heard for several hundred li, and wild pheasants all crowed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a stone drum in Jixian boomed for hundreds of li and pheasants called without cease.

sentences.zh: 秦州地震者三十二，殷殷有聲者八，山崩舍壞，咸以為不祥。

translations.literal: In Qinzhou there were thirty-two earthquakes with rumbling sound in eight cases; mountains collapsed and houses ruined—all thought it inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou then suffered dozens of quakes, rockslides, and ruined homes—everyone called it an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 及嵩將出，群僚固諫止之。

translations.literal: When Song was about to set out, the host of officials firmly remonstrated to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Song prepared to march, the court begged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「若有不祥，此乃命也，安所逃乎！

translations.literal: Song said, "If there is inauspiciousness, this is fate—where would one flee!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Song said, "If doom comes, it is fate—there is no escape."

sentences.zh: 」遂及於難。

translations.literal: Thereupon he met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He rode to his death.

sentences.zh: 識者以為秦州泓之故鄉，將滅之征也。

translations.literal: Those with insight thought Qinzhou was Hong's old homeland—an omen of its about to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Wise men said Qinzhou was Yao Hong's home ground—its ruin foretold his own.

sentences.zh: 赫連勃勃攻陷陰密，執秦州刺史姚軍都，坑將士五千餘人。

translations.literal: Helian Bobo attacked and took Yinmi, seized Qinzhou Inspector Yao Jundu, and buried alive more than five thousand officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo stormed Yinmi, captured Yao Jundu, and slaughtered over five thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 軍都瞋目厲聲數勃勃殘忍之罪，不為之屈，勃勃怒而殺之。

translations.literal: Jundu glared with eyes and in stern voice enumerated Bobo's crimes of cruelty and refused to yield to him; Bobo in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Jundu glared and cursed Bobo's cruelty to his face; Bobo slew him in rage.

sentences.zh: 勃勃既克陰密，進兵侵雍，嶺北雜戶悉奔五將山。

translations.literal: Once Bobo had taken Yinmi, he advanced troops to invade Yong; north-of-the-ridge miscellaneous households all fled to Five-General Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After Yinmi, Bobo struck toward Yong and drove every northern household toward Five-General Mountain.

sentences.zh: 征北姚恢棄安定，率戶五千奔新平，安定人胡儼、華韜等率眾距恢，恢單騎歸長安。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North Yao Hui abandoned Anding, led five thousand households to flee to Xinping; Anding men Hu Yan and Hua Tao led hosts to block Hui; Hui alone on horseback returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hui quit Anding with five thousand households for Xinping; local leaders blocked him and he galloped alone back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 立節彌姐成、建武裴岐為儼所殺，鎮西姚諶委鎮東走。

translations.literal: Jianjie Mijie Cheng and Jianwu Pei Qi were killed by Yan; General Who Guards the West Yao Chen abandoned the garrison and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: Mijie Cheng and Pei Qi died fighting Hu Yan; Yao Chen abandoned his post and ran east.

sentences.zh: 勃勃遂據雍，抄掠郿城。

translations.literal: Bobo thereupon occupied Yong, raiding and plundering Mei city.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo then overran Yong and raided Mei.

sentences.zh: 姚紹及征虜尹昭、鎮軍姚洽等率步騎五萬討勃勃，姚恢以精騎一萬繼之。

translations.literal: Yao Shao and General Who Captures Barbarians Yin Zhao, General Who Guards the Army Yao Qia, and others led fifty thousand foot and horse to campaign against Bobo; Yao Hui with ten thousand picked cavalry followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao, Yin Zhao, and Yao Qia led fifty thousand men against Bobo; Yao Hui followed with ten thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 軍次橫水，勃勃退保安定，胡儼閉門距之，殺鮮卑數千人，據安定以降。

translations.literal: The army halted at Hengshui; Bobo withdrew to guard Anding; Hu Yan closed the gate to block him, killed several thousand Xianbei, and occupied Anding to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengshui Bobo pulled back to Anding; Hu Yan shut the gates, killed thousands of Xianbei, and handed the city over.

sentences.zh: 紹進兵躡勃勃，戰於馬鞍阪，敗之，追至朝那，不及而還。

translations.literal: Shao advanced the army to tread on Bobo, fought at Ma'an Slope, defeated him, pursued to Zhaona, did not catch up and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao beat Bobo at Ma'an Ridge, chased him toward Zhaona, then broke off the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 楊盛遣兄子倦入寇長蛇。

translations.literal: Yang Sheng sent his elder brother's son Juan to invade Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng sent his nephew Yang Juan against Changshe.

sentences.zh: 平陽氐苟渴聚眾千餘，據五丈原以叛，遣鎮遠姚萬、恢武姚難討之，為渴所敗。

translations.literal: Pingyang Di Gou Ke gathered more than a thousand, occupied Wuzhangyuan in revolt; he sent General Who Guards the Distance Yao Wan and General Who Restores Might Yao Nan to campaign against him, and they were defeated by Ke.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chief Gou Ke seized Wuzhangyuan; Yao Wan and Yao Nan marched against him and lost.

sentences.zh: 姚諶討渴，擒之。

translations.literal: Yao Chen campaigned against Ke and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chen captured Gou Ke in a second expedition.

sentences.zh: 泓使輔國斂曼嵬、前將軍姚光兒討楊倦于陳倉，倦奔于散關。

translations.literal: Hong sent General Who Supports the State Lian Mankui and Forward General Yao Guang'er to campaign against Yang Juan at Cangcang; Juan fled to Sanguan.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Lian Mankui and Yao Guang'er to Cangcang; Yang Juan bolted for Sanguan.

sentences.zh: 勃勃遣兄子提南侵池陽，車騎姚裕、前將軍彭白狼、建義蛇玄距卻之。

translations.literal: Bobo sent his elder brother's son Ti south to raid Chiyang; chariots and cavalry Yao Yu, Forward General Peng Bailang, and Jianyi She Xuan blocked him and drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo's nephew Ti raided Chiyang but Yao Yu, Peng Bailang, and She Xuan threw him back.

sentences.zh: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓，次於彭城，遣冠軍將軍檀道濟、龍驤將軍王鎮惡入自淮、肥，攻漆丘、項城，將軍沈林子自汴入河，攻倉垣。

translations.literal: Before long Jin Grand Commandant Liu Yu commanded the great host to campaign against Hong, halted at Pengcheng, sent General Who Wins the Championship Tan Daoji and General Who Soars like Dragon Wang Zhen'e in from Huai and Fei to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng, General Shen Linzi from Bian into the He to attack Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Yu of Jin massed at Pengcheng and sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen'e through Huai-Fei against Qiqiu and Xiangcheng while Shen Linzi struck Cangyuan from Bian.

sentences.zh: 泓將王苟生以漆丘降鎮惡，徐州刺史姚掌以項城降道濟，王師遂入潁口，所至多降服。

translations.literal: Hong's general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Zhen'e; Xuzhou Inspector Yao Zhang surrendered Xiangcheng to Daoji; the royal army then entered Yingkou, and wherever it went there was surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gousheng yielded Qiqiu to Wang Zhen'e, Yao Zhang yielded Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji, and the Jin host poured through Yingkou almost unopposed.

sentences.zh: 惟新蔡太守董遵固守不降，道濟攻破之，縛遵而致諸軍門。

translations.literal: Only Xin'cai Grand Administrator Dong Zun firmly guarded and would not surrender; Daoji broke him, bound Zun, and brought him to the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Only Dong Zun of Xin'cai held out until Tan Daoji stormed the city and bound him before the camp.

sentences.zh: 遵厲色曰：「古之王者伐國，待士以禮。

translations.literal: Zun in stern color said, "Kings of old in campaigning against states treated knights with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zun snapped: "Ancient kings campaigned with courtesy toward worthy foes.

sentences.zh: 君奈何以不義行師，待國土以非禮乎。

translations.literal: How can you, sir, march with unrighteous conduct and treat a state's knights without ritual."
translations.idiomatic: How dare you wage an unjust war and dishonor a loyal governor?"

sentences.zh: 」道濟怒殺之。

translations.literal: Daoji in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji killed him in fury.

sentences.zh: 姚紹聞王師之至，還長安，言於泓曰：「晉師已過許昌，豫州、安定孤遠，卒難救衛，宜遷諸鎮戶內實京畿，可得精兵十萬，足以橫行天下。

translations.literal: When Yao Shao heard the royal army had arrived, he returned to Chang'an and said to Hong, "The Jin army has passed Xuchang; Yuzhou and Anding are isolated and far; in the end hard to rescue—it is fitting to move the garrison households inward to fill the capital region; you can obtain crack troops of one hundred thousand, enough to range across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao raced back to warn Yao Hong: "Jin is past Xuchang—Yuzhou and Anding are too far to save. Move frontier households into the capital for a hundred thousand veterans."

sentences.zh: 假使二寇交侵，無深害也。

translations.literal: Even if the two bandits jointly invade, there is no deep harm.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Bobo and Jin strike together, a thick core can absorb the blow.

sentences.zh: 如其不爾，晉侵豫州，勃勃寇安定者，將若之何！

translations.literal: If it is not so—Jin invading Yuzhou and Bobo raiding Anding—what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Jin will chew Yuzhou while Bobo gnaws Anding—what then?"

sentences.zh: 事機已至，宜在速決。

translations.literal: The moment of affairs has arrived; it is fitting to decide with speed."
translations.idiomatic: The hour demands a fast decision."

sentences.zh: 」其左僕射梁喜曰：「齊公恢雄勇有威名，為嶺北所憚，鎮人已與勃勃深仇，理應守死無貳，勃勃終不能棄安定遠寇京畿。

translations.literal: His left vice-director Liang Xi said, "Duke of Qi Hui is fierce and brave and has an awesome name, feared north of the ridge; the garrison people already have deep hatred with Bobo, by principle ought to guard unto death without second mind—Bobo in the end cannot abandon Anding and raid the capital region far.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi argued: "Yao Hui terrifies the north; his garrisons hate Bobo and will die before yielding—Bobo cannot skip Anding to strike the core."

sentences.zh: 若無安定，虜馬必及於郿、雍。

translations.literal: If there is no Anding, enemy horses will surely reach Mei and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Lose Anding and enemy horsemen will reach Mei and Yong.

sentences.zh: 今關中兵馬足距晉師，豈可未有憂危先自削損也。

translations.literal: Now Guanzhong troops and horses are enough to stop the Jin army—how can one, not yet having worry and peril, first wound oneself by cutting away!"
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong can still face Jin—why cripple yourself before the crisis?"

sentences.zh: 」泓從之。

translations.literal: Hong followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sided with Liang Xi.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎懿橫密言於泓曰：「齊公恢于廣平之難有忠勳于陛下，自陛下龍飛紹統，未有殊賞以答其意。

translations.literal: Personnel Director Yi Heng secretly said to Hong, "Duke of Qi Hui at the Guangping crisis had loyal merit toward Your Majesty; since Your Majesty's dragon flight and succession, there has been no special reward to answer his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel clerk Yi Heng whispered: "Yao Hui saved you at Guangping yet has never been richly rewarded."

sentences.zh: 今外則致之死地，內則不豫朝權，安定人自以孤危逼寇，欲思南遷者十室而九，若擁精兵四萬，鼓行而向京師，得不為社稷之累乎！

translations.literal: Now outside he is cast into a dead place, inside he does not share court power; Anding men themselves think isolated and endangered by the raider—those who wish to think of moving south are nine houses in ten—if he rallies crack troops of forty thousand and drums his march toward the capital, could it not be a burden on the altars!
translations.idiomatic: Now he is stranded abroad without voice at court; Anding feels doomed—nine tenths want to flee south. Give him forty thousand veterans and he could drum straight on Chang'an—think of the risk!"

sentences.zh: 宜征還朝廷，以慰其心。

translations.literal: It is fitting to summon him back to court to comfort his mind."
translations.idiomatic: Recall him to the capital to calm him."

sentences.zh: 」泓曰：「恢若懷不逞之心，征之適所以速禍耳。

translations.literal: Hong said, "If Hui harbors a mind of unfulfilled ambition, summoning him would only hasten disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong said: "If Yao Hui is disloyal, recalling him would only hasten revolt."

sentences.zh: 」又不從。

translations.literal: Again he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: He refused again.

sentences.zh: 王師至成皋，征南姚洸時鎮洛陽，馳使請救。

translations.literal: When the royal army reached Chenggao, General Who Conquers the South Yao Guang then garrisoned Luoyang, sent dispatch riders requesting rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin reached Chenggao, Yao Guang in Luoyang begged for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 泓遣越騎校尉閻生率騎三千以赴之，武衛姚益男將步卒一萬助守洛陽，又遣征東、并州牧姚懿南屯陝津為之聲援。

translations.literal: Hong sent Colonel of Agile Cavalry Yan Sheng with three thousand horse to hurry there, Martial Guard Yao Yinan leading ten thousand foot soldiers to assist in guarding Luoyang, and also sent General Who Conquers the East and shepherd of Bingzhou Yao Yi to camp south at Shan ford as sounding support.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Yan Sheng with three thousand horse, Yao Yinan with ten thousand foot to Luoyang, and Yao Yi to Shan ford as a screen.

sentences.zh: 洸部將趙玄說洸曰：「今寇逼已深，百姓駭懼，眾寡勢殊，難以應敵。

translations.literal: Guang's subordinate Zhao Xuan spoke to Guang, saying, "Now the raider's pressure is already deep, the hundred surnames are terrified; few and many, the power situation is unequal—hard to answer the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xuan warned Yao Guang: "The enemy is on top of us, the people panic, and we are outnumbered."

sentences.zh: 宜攝諸戍兵士，固守金墉，以待京師之援，不可出戰。

translations.literal: You ought to gather the garrison soldiers and firmly guard the Metal Rampart, awaiting rescue from the capital region; you must not go out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Pull every defender behind the Metal Rampart and wait for relief from Chang'an—do not offer battle outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 如脫不捷，大事去矣。

translations.literal: If perchance you are not victorious, the great enterprise is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Lose that fight and the cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 金墉既固，師無損敗，吳寇終不敢越金墉而西。

translations.literal: Once Metal Rampart is firm, the army suffers no defeat, and the Wu bandits in the end dare not cross Metal Rampart westward.
translations.idiomatic: Hold that fortress and Jin will never dare push west of it.

sentences.zh: 困之於堅城之下，可以坐制其弊。

translations.literal: Trap them beneath a strong city; you can sit and control their exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Starve them under your walls without lifting another spear.

sentences.zh: 」時洸司馬姚禹潛通於道濟，主簿閻恢、楊虔等皆禹之党，嫉玄忠誠，咸共毀之，固勸洸出戰。

translations.literal: At that time Guang's Major Yao Yu secretly communicated with Daoji; chief clerk Yan Hui and Yang Qian and others were all Yu's faction, jealous of Xuan's loyalty, together slandered him, and firmly urged Guang to go out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yu plotted with Tan Daoji's party; jealous officers smeared Zhao Xuan and pushed Yao Guang to march out.

sentences.zh: 洸從之，乃遣玄率精兵千餘南守柏穀塢，廣武石無諱東戍鞏城，以距王師。

translations.literal: Guang followed them, then sent Xuan leading more than a thousand picked troops south to guard the Bai Valley stockade, Guangwu Shi Wuhui east to guard Gong city, to block the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guang listened: he sent Zhao Xuan to Bai Valley and Shi Wuhui to Gong to block Jin.

sentences.zh: 玄泣謂洸曰：「玄受三帝重恩，所守正死耳。

translations.literal: Xuan wept and said to Guang, "Xuan has received triple favor from three emperors—what I hold is only death."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xuan wept: "Three emperors favored me—I mean to die loyally here."

sentences.zh: 但明公不用忠臣之言，為奸孽所誤，後必悔之，但無及耳。

translations.literal: But the enlightened lord does not use loyal ministers' words, is misled by evil spawn—later you will regret it, but it will not be in time!"
translations.idiomatic: You spurn loyal counsel for flatterers—you will regret this when it is too late!"

sentences.zh: 」會陽城及成皋、滎陽、武牢諸城悉降，道濟等長驅而至。

translations.literal: When Yangcheng and Chenggao, Xingyang, Wulao citadels all surrendered, Daoji and others drove straight through.
translations.idiomatic: Yangcheng, Chenggao, Xingyang, and Wulao fell; Tan Daoji rolled forward unchecked.

sentences.zh: 無諱至石關，奔還。

translations.literal: Wuhui reached Stone Pass and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wuhui broke at Stone Pass and ran.

sentences.zh: 玄與晉將毛德祖戰于柏穀，以眾寡而敗，被瘡十餘，據地大呼，玄司馬騫鑒冒刃抱玄而泣，玄曰：「吾瘡已重，君宜速去。

translations.literal: Xuan fought Jin general Mao Dezu at Baigu; because few against many he was defeated, received more than ten wounds, clutched the ground and shouted; Xuan's Major Qian Jian braved blades, embraced Xuan and wept; Xuan said, "My wounds are already heavy—you ought quickly to depart."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xuan fought Mao Dezu at Baigu, was overrun and cut down; Qian Jian tried to drag him clear but Zhao said, "I am finished—save yourself."

sentences.zh: 」鑒曰：「若將軍不濟，當與俱死，去將安之！

translations.literal: Qian said, "If the general does not succeed, I should die with you—where would I go leaving!"
translations.idiomatic: Qian Jian said, "If you fall, I fall with you."

sentences.zh: 」皆死於陣。

translations.literal: Both died in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Both died on the field.

sentences.zh: 姚禹逾城奔于王師。

translations.literal: Yao Yu climbed the wall and fled to the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yu went over the wall to Jin.

sentences.zh: 道濟進至洛陽、洸懼，遂降。

translations.literal: Daoji advanced to Luoyang; Guang feared and then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji reached Luoyang; Yao Guang surrendered in panic.

sentences.zh: 時閻生至新安，益男至湖城，會洛陽已沒，遂留屯不進。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Sheng had reached Xin'an, Yinan had reached Hucheng; when Luoyang had already fallen, they therefore halted and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Sheng and Yao Yinan stopped cold when they heard Luoyang was lost.

sentences.zh: 姚懿嶮薄，惑於信受，其司馬孫暢奸巧傾佞，好亂樂禍，勸懿襲長安，誅姚紹，廢泓自立。

translations.literal: Yao Yi was perilous and mean, deluded by what he trusted; his Major Sun Chang was crafty, fawning, fond of turmoil and rejoicing in disaster, urging Yi to raid Chang'an, kill Yao Shao, depose Hong and set himself up.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yao Yi was vain and credulous; Sun Chang urged him to strike Chang'an, kill Yao Shao, and seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 懿納之，乃引兵至陝津，散谷以賜河北夷夏，欲虛損國儲，招引和戎諸羌，樹已私惠。

translations.literal: Yi accepted it, then led troops to Shan ford, scattered grain to give to Hebei Yi and Xia of every sort, wishing to hollow out state stores, summon and win the peace-with-barbarians Qiang, and plant private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi marched to Shan ford and scattered state grain to buy tribal loyalty.

sentences.zh: 懿左常侍張敞、侍郎左雅固諫懿曰：「殿下以母弟之親，居分陝之重，安危休戚，與國共之。

translations.literal: Yi's left constant attendant Zhang Chang and attendant Zuo Ya firmly remonstrated Yi, saying, "Your Highness, with the closeness of mother's-brother kin, holds the weight of dividing Shaan; safety and peril, rest and sorrow, you share with the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang and Zuo Ya warned: "You are the emperor's uncle on the western front—your fate is the dynasty's fate.

sentences.zh: 漢有七國之難，實賴梁王。

translations.literal: Han had the disaster of the seven states—it truly relied on the Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Han survived the Seven Kingdoms revolt because the Prince of Liang stood firm.

sentences.zh: 今吳寇內侵，四州傾沒，西虜擾邊，秦、涼覆敗，朝廷之危有同累卵，正是諸侯勤王之日。

translations.literal: Now the Wu bandit invades within, four provinces have toppled, western raiders disturb the border, Qin and Liang are overthrown—the court's peril is like piled eggs; this is exactly the day when lords should aid the king.
translations.idiomatic: Jin is inside the passes, four provinces are gone, Bobo tears the west—this is the hour to rally for the throne, not to hoard grain.

sentences.zh: 谷者，國之本也，而今散之。

translations.literal: Grain is the state's root, yet now you scatter it.
translations.idiomatic: Grain is the root of power, and you are pouring it away.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷問殿下者，將何辭以報？

translations.literal: If the court asks Your Highness, with what words will you answer?"
translations.idiomatic: What will you tell the emperor when he asks where the granaries went?"

sentences.zh: 」懿怒，笞而殺之。

translations.literal: Yi in anger flogged and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi had them beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 泓聞之，召姚紹等密謀於朝堂。

translations.literal: When Hong heard it, he summoned Yao Shao and others to plot secretly in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong called Yao Shao into the palace for a secret council.

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「懿性識鄙近，從物推移，造成此事，惟當孫暢耳。

translations.literal: Shao said, "Yi's nature and insight are base and near, following things as they shift; what made this affair is only Sun Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao said: "Yao Yi is weak-minded; Sun Chang made him do this.

sentences.zh: 但馳使征暢，遣撫軍贊據陝城，臣向潼關為諸軍節度，若暢奉詔而至者，臣當遣懿率河東見兵共平吳寇。

translations.literal: Only dispatch riders at speed to summon Chang; send General Who Pacifies Zan to hold Shan city; I will go to Tong Pass to command all armies—if Chang comes bearing the edict, I will order Yi to lead Hedong's available troops together to pacify the Wu bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Arrest Sun Chang, put Yao Zan in Shan, and I will take Tong Pass—if they obey, Yao Yi can still march east against Jin.

sentences.zh: 如其逆釁已成，違距詔敕者，當明其罪於天下，聲鼓以擊之。

translations.literal: If their rebellious rift is already formed and they defy the edict, then make their crime clear to the realm and beat the drums to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: If they defy the edict, publish their treason and attack."

sentences.zh: 」泓曰：「叔父之言，社稷之計也。

translations.literal: Hong said, "Uncle's words are the plan for the altars."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong said, "Uncle, your plan saves the state."

sentences.zh: 」於是遣姚贊及冠軍司馬國璠、建義蛇玄屯陝津，武衛姚驢屯潼關。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Yao Zan and champion major Simo Guofan, Jianyi She Xuan to camp at Shan ford, Martial Guard Yao Lü to camp at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yao Zan, Simo Guofan, and She Xuan to Shan and Yao Lü to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 懿遂舉兵僭號，傳檄州郡，欲運匈奴堡穀以給鎮人。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon raised troops and presumptuously assumed title, circulated call to arms to province and commandery, wished to transport Xiongnu Fort grain to supply the garrison men.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi declared himself ruler and tried to ship grain from Xiongnu Fort to his troops.

sentences.zh: 甯東姚成都距之，懿乃卑辭招誘，深自結托，送佩刀為誓，成都送以呈泓。

translations.literal: General Who Calms the East Yao Chengdu blocked him; Yi then used humble words to entice and win him, deeply pledged himself, sent a belt knife as oath—Chengdu sent it to present to Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chengdu blocked him; Yao Yi tried flattery and sent a pledge knife—Chengdu handed it to Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: 懿又遣驍騎王國率甲士數百攻成都，成都擒國，囚之，遣讓懿曰：「明公以母弟之親，受推轂之寄，今社稷之危若綴旒然，宜恭恪憂勤，匡輔王室。

translations.literal: Yi also sent swift cavalry Wang Guo leading several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu; Chengdu seized Guo, imprisoned him, sent reproach to Yi, saying, "The enlightened lord, with mother's-brother closeness, received the charge of the pushing-bar wheel; now the altars' peril hangs like a tassel—he ought reverently to toil in worry and assist the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu captured Wang Guo and scolded Yao Yi: "As the emperor's uncle you should steady the throne, not plot treason.

sentences.zh: 而更包藏奸宄，謀危宗廟，三祖之靈豈安公乎！

translations.literal: Yet you harbor treachery and plot danger to the ancestral temple—can the spirits of the three ancestors rest easy with you!
translations.idiomatic: The imperial ancestors will not bless a traitor.

sentences.zh: 此鎮之糧，一方所寄，鎮人何功，而欲給之！

translations.literal: This garrison's grain is what one region relies on—what merit have garrison men that you wish to supply them!
translations.idiomatic: This grain feeds the frontier—what right have you to give it away?

sentences.zh: 王國為蛇畫足，國之罪人，已就囚執，聽詔而戮之。

translations.literal: Wang Guo was a snake painting feet—a criminal of the state; he is already imprisoned awaiting the edict to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo was a fool's errand; he waits in chains for the axe.

sentences.zh: 成都方糾合義眾，以懲明公之罪，復須大兵悉集，當與明公會於河上。

translations.literal: Chengdu is now gathering righteous hosts to punish the enlightened lord's crime; again must great hosts all assemble—I will meet the enlightened lord on the river.
translations.idiomatic: I am raising loyal troops to meet you on the Yellow River."

sentences.zh: 」乃宣告諸城，勉以忠義，厲兵秣馬，徵發義租。

translations.literal: Thereupon he proclaimed to the cities, urged them with loyalty and righteousness, sharpened weapons and fed horses, and levied righteous rent.
translations.idiomatic: He called the garrisons to arms and gathered supplies.

sentences.zh: 河東之兵無詣懿者，懿深患之。

translations.literal: Not one Hedong soldier went to Yi; Yi deeply worried over it.
translations.idiomatic: No Hedong troops joined Yao Yi; he panicked.

sentences.zh: 臨晉數千戶叛應懿。

translations.literal: Several thousand households of Linjin rebelled to answer Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands in Linjin rose for him.

sentences.zh: 姚紹濟自薄津，擊臨晉叛戶，大破之，懿等震懼。

translations.literal: Yao Shao crossed from Bo ford, struck the Linjin rebel households, greatly defeated them; Yi and others were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao crossed at Bo ford, crushed the Linjin rebels, and terrified Yao Yi.

sentences.zh: 鎮人安定郭純、王奴等率眾圍懿。

translations.literal: Garrison men of Anding Guo Chun and Wang Nu and others led hosts to surround Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chun and Wang Nu besieged Yao Yi.

sentences.zh: 紹入于蒲阪，執懿囚之，誅孫暢等。

translations.literal: Shao entered Puban, seized Yi and imprisoned him, executed Sun Chang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao took Puban, jailed Yao Yi, and executed Sun Chang.

sentences.zh: 泓以內外離叛，王師漸逼，歲旦朝群臣於其前殿，淒然流涕，群臣皆泣。

translations.literal: Because inner and outer split in rebellion and the royal army pressed gradually, on New Year's dawn Hong met the host of ministers in his front hall, wept dismally; the host of ministers all wept.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day Yao Hong wept before his court as Jin closed in and kin rebelled.

sentences.zh: 時征北姚恢率安定鎮戶三萬八千，焚燒室宇，以車為方陣，自北雍州趣長安，自稱大都督、建義大將軍，移檄州郡，欲除君側之惡。

translations.literal: At the time General Who Conquers the North Yao Hui led thirty-eight thousand Anding garrison households, burned houses, formed a chariot square, went from North Yongzhou toward Chang'an, styled himself grand commander-in-chief and great general who establishes righteousness, circulated call to arms to province and commandery, wishing to remove evil beside the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hui marched on Chang'an with thirty-eight thousand families in chariot fortresses, claiming he would purge evil counselors.

sentences.zh: 揚威姜紀率眾奔之。

translations.literal: General Who Displays Might Jiang Ji led hosts to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji rode to his banner.

sentences.zh: 建節彭完都聞恢將至，棄陰密，奔還長安。

translations.literal: Jianjie Peng Wandu heard Hui would arrive, abandoned Yinmi, fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Wandu fled Yinmi for the capital.

sentences.zh: 恢至新支，姜紀說恢曰：「國家重將在東，京師空虛，公可輕兵徑襲，事必克矣。

translations.literal: When Hui reached Xin-zhi, Jiang Ji urged Hui, saying, "The state's weighty generals are east; the capital is empty—with light troops you could raid straight in; the affair would surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji urged a coup de main on empty Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 」恢不從，乃南攻郿城。

translations.literal: Hui did not follow, then attacked south toward Mei city.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hui refused and struck south for Mei instead.

sentences.zh: 鎮西姚諶為恢所敗，恢軍勢彌盛，長安大震。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the West Yao Chen was defeated by Hui; Hui's army momentum grew ever stronger; Chang'an was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chen lost to Yao Hui; panic gripped Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 泓馳使征紹，遣姚裕及輔國胡翼度屯於灃西。

translations.literal: Hong dispatched riders summoning Shao, sent Yao Yu and General Who Supports the State Hu Yidu to camp west of the Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong recalled Yao Shao and sent Yao Yu and Hu Yidu west of the Feng River.

sentences.zh: 扶風太守姚雋、安夷護軍姚墨蠡、建威姚娥都、揚威彭蠔皆懼而降恢。

translations.literal: Fufeng Grand Administrator Yao Jun, Protector of the Pacified Yi Yao Moli, Jianwei Yao E'du, General Who Displays Might Peng Hao all feared and surrendered to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Several frontier generals went over to Yao Hui.

sentences.zh: 恢舅苟和時為立節將軍，守忠不貳，泓召而謂之曰：「眾人咸懷去就，卿何能自安邪？

translations.literal: Hui's maternal uncle Gou He then served as Jianjie general, kept loyalty without wavering; Hong summoned him and said, "The multitude all harbor leaving or staying—how can you alone be at ease?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong asked Gou He why he stayed loyal while kin rebelled.

sentences.zh: 」和曰：「若天縱妖賊，得肆其逆節者，舅甥之理，不待賓士而加親。

translations.literal: He said, "If Heaven lets the demon bandit prevail and he gets to carry out his treason, the principle of uncle and nephew needs no guest-retainer to grow closer.
translations.idiomatic: Gou He said: "If treason wins, uncle and nephew share the stain.

sentences.zh: 如其罪極逆銷，天盈其罰者，守忠執志，臣之體也。

translations.literal: If his crime reaches its limit and treason melts, Heaven filling his punishment, keeping loyalty and holding resolve—that is the body of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven punishes the traitor, a subject stands by his oath.

sentences.zh: 違親叛君，臣之所恥。

translations.literal: To violate kin and betray the lord is what a subject shames.
translations.idiomatic: Betraying sovereign for kin would shame me."

sentences.zh: 」泓善其忠恕，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: Hong praised his loyal forgiveness and added gold seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong honored him with gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 姚紹率輕騎先赴難，使姚洽、司馬國璠將步卒三萬赴長安。

translations.literal: Yao Shao led light horse first to the crisis, sent Yao Qia and Simo Guofan leading thirty thousand foot to hurry to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao raced ahead while Yao Qia and Guofan brought thirty thousand foot toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 恢從曲牢進屯杜成，紹與恢相持於靈台。

translations.literal: Hui advanced from Qulao and camped at Ducheng; Shao and Hui faced each other at Lingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hui camped at Ducheng; Yao Shao met him at Lingtai.

sentences.zh: 姚贊聞恢漸逼，留甯朔尹雅為弘農太守，守潼關，率諸軍還長安。

translations.literal: When Zan heard Hui pressed gradually, he left Ningyin Yin Ya as Hongnong grand administrator guarding Tong Pass, led all armies back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan rushed back from Tong Pass, leaving Yin Ya to hold the river.

sentences.zh: 泓謝贊曰：「元子不能崇明德義，導率群下，致禍起蕭牆，變自同氣，既上負祖宗，亦無顏見諸父。

translations.literal: Hong thanked Zan, saying, "Yuanzi cannot brighten virtue and righteousness or lead the host below, causing disaster to rise from the inner wall and change to come from same-blood kin—already above I fail the ancestors, below I have no face to see the uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong told Yao Zan: "I have failed the ancestors and shamed my uncles with these kin revolts.

sentences.zh: 懿始構逆滅亡，恢復擁眾內叛，將若之何？

translations.literal: Yi first plotted rebellion and perished; Hui again embraces hosts in inner rebellion—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi is dead yet Yao Hui marches on the capital—what now?"

sentences.zh: 」贊曰：「懿等所以敢稱兵內侮者，諒由臣等輕弱，無防遏之方故也。

translations.literal: Zan said, "The reason Yi and others dared raise arms in inner insult is surely because we ministers are weak and light, without means to prevent and block.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan said: "They rebelled because we ministers seemed weak.

sentences.zh: 」因攘袂大泣曰：「臣與大將軍不滅此賊，終不持面復見陛下！

translations.literal: Thereupon he pulled his sleeve and wept greatly, saying, "Your subject with the grand general will not destroy these bandits—never again shall I hold face to see Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: He swore with Yao Shao to kill the traitors or never face the throne again.

sentences.zh: 」泓於是班賜軍士而遣之。

translations.literal: Hong thereupon distributed gifts to the army soldiers and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong paid the troops and sent them out.

sentences.zh: 恢眾見諸軍悉集，咸懼而思善，其將齊黃等棄恢而降。

translations.literal: Hui's host seeing all armies assembled all feared and thought of good; his generals Qi Huang and others abandoned Hui and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hui's men wavered; Qi Huang and others defected.

sentences.zh: 恢進軍逼紹，贊自後要擊，大破之，殺恢及其三弟。

translations.literal: Hui advanced the army pressing Shao; Zan struck him from the rear, greatly defeated him, killed Hui and his three younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan fell on Yao Hui from the rear, killed him and three brothers.

sentences.zh: 泓哭之悲慟，葬以公禮。

translations.literal: Hong wept for him with extreme grief and buried him with ducal rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong buried him with princely honors and mourned bitterly.

sentences.zh: 至是，王鎮惡至宜陽。

translations.literal: By this time Wang Zhen'e had reached Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e had reached Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 毛德祖攻弘農太守尹雅于蠡城，眾潰，德祖使騎追獲之，既而殺晉守者奔固潼關。

translations.literal: Mao Dezu attacked Hongnong Grand Administrator Yin Ya at Li city; the host broke; Dezu sent cavalry pursuing and seized him; afterward he killed the Jin guards and fled to firm Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dezu broke Yin Ya at Li, captured him, killed Jin guards, and fled to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟、沈林子攻拔襄邑堡，建威薛帛奔河東。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi attacked and took Xiangyi stockade; Jianwei Xue Bo fled to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi took Xiangyi; Xue Bo ran to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 道濟白陝北渡，攻蒲阪，使將軍苟卓攻匈奴堡，為泓甯東姚成都所敗。

translations.literal: Daoji crossed north from Shan, attacked Puban, sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort, and was defeated by Hong's General Who Calms the East Yao Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji crossed north against Puban; Gou Zhuo lost to Yao Chengdu at Xiongnu Fort.

sentences.zh: 泓遣姚驢救蒲阪，胡翼度據潼關。

translations.literal: Hong sent Yao Lü to rescue Puban; Hu Yidu held Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Yao Lü to Puban and Hu Yidu held Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 泓進紹太宰、大將軍、大都督、都督中外諸軍事、假黃鋮，改封魯公，侍中、司隸、宗正、節錄並如故，朝之大政皆往決焉。

translations.literal: Hong advanced Shao to grand tutor, grand general, grand commander-in-chief, commander of all military affairs within and without, granted yellow battle-axe, changed enfeoffment to duke of Lu—palace attendant, director of Sizhou, director of clan affairs, holding seal and tallies as before; great court policy all went to decide there.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong made Yao Shao supreme commander with the yellow axe and Lu dukedom, leaving all war policy to him.

sentences.zh: 紹固辭，弗許。

translations.literal: Shao firmly declined; he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao refused the honors; Yao Hong insisted.

sentences.zh: 於是遣紹率武衛姚鸞等步騎五萬，距王師於潼關。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Shao leading Martial Guard Yao Luan and others, fifty thousand foot and horse, to block the royal army at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yao Shao with fifty thousand men to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 姚驢與并州刺史尹昭為表裏之勢，夾攻道濟。

translations.literal: Yao Lü and Bingzhou Inspector Yin Zhao formed inner-outer posture and jointly attacked Daoji.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lü and Yin Zhao hit Tan Daoji from two sides.

sentences.zh: 道濟深壁不戰，沈林子說道濟曰：「今蒲阪城堅池浚，非可卒克，攻之傷眾，守之引日，不如棄之，先事潼關。

translations.literal: Daoji kept deep walls and did not fight; Shen Linzi persuaded Daoji, saying, "Now Puban city is firm and moat deep—not to be taken in haste; attacking it wounds the host, guarding it draws out days—better to abandon it and first strike Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linzi urged Tan Daoji to abandon Puban for Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 潼關天限，形勝之地，鎮惡孤軍，勢危力寡，若使姚紹據之，則難圖矣。

translations.literal: Tong Pass is Heaven's barrier, a place of terrain's advantage; Zhen'e is an isolated army, situation perilous and force small—if you let Yao Shao hold it, it will be hard to plan.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Pass is the bottleneck; if Yao Shao locks it, Wang Zhen'e is lost.

sentences.zh: 如克潼關，紹可不戰而服。

translations.literal: If you take Tong Pass, Shao can be subdued without battle."
translations.idiomatic: Seize the pass and Yao Shao will fold without another fight."

sentences.zh: 」道濟從之，乃棄蒲阪，南向潼關。

translations.literal: Daoji followed it, then abandoned Puban and went south toward Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji gave up Puban and marched on Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 姚贊率禁兵七千，自渭北而東，進據蒲津。

translations.literal: Yao Zan led seven thousand household troops from north of the Wei eastward and advanced to occupy Pu ford.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan took seven thousand palace guards to Pu ford.

sentences.zh: 劉裕使沈田子及傅弘之率眾萬餘人入上洛，所在多委城鎮奔長安。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi leading more than ten thousand to enter Shangluo; place after place mostly abandoned cities and towns and fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi into Shangluo; towns collapsed toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 田子等進及青泥，姚紹方陣而前，以距道濟。

translations.literal: Tianzi and others advanced as far as Qingni; Yao Shao formed square array and advanced to block Daoji.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tianzi reached Qingni while Yao Shao advanced to face Tan Daoji.

sentences.zh: 道濟固壘不戰，紹乃攻其西營，不克，遂以大眾逼之。

translations.literal: Daoji kept firm ramparts and did not fight; Shao then attacked his western camp, did not take it, then pressed with the great host.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji stayed behind walls; Yao Shao stormed his west camp, failed, then massed against him.

sentences.zh: 道濟率王敬、沈林子等逆沖紹軍，將士驚散，引還定城。

translations.literal: Daoji led Wang Chong, Shen Linzi and others to charge straight at Shao's army; officers and soldiers startled and scattered, drew back to Dingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji counterattacked but broke and withdrew to Dingcheng.

sentences.zh: 紹留姚鸞守險，絕道濟糧道。

translations.literal: Shao left Yao Luan guarding the narrows, cutting Daoji's grain road.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao left Yao Luan to choke Tan Daoji's supply line.

sentences.zh: 時裕別將姚珍入自子午，竇霸入自洛穀，眾各數千人。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Yu's separate general Yao Zhen entered from Ziwu, Dou Ba entered from Luogu, each several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's columns entered from Ziwu and Luogu valleys.

sentences.zh: 泓遣姚萬距霸，姚彊距珍。

translations.literal: Hong sent Yao Wan to block Ba, Yao Qiang to block Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Yao Wan and Yao Qiang to meet them.

sentences.zh: 姚鸞遣將尹雅與道濟司馬徐琰于潼關南，為琰所獲，送之劉裕。

translations.literal: Yao Luan sent general Yin Ya with Daoji's major Xu Yan south of Tong Pass; he was seized by Yan and sent to Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ya was captured by Xu Yan and sent to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕以雅前叛，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Yu because Ya had formerly rebelled, wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu meant to execute Yin Ya for past treason.

sentences.zh: 雅曰：「前活本在望外，今死寧不甘心。

translations.literal: Ya said, "Formerly living was already beyond expectation; now death surely I do not willingly accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ya said: "You spared me once; now I will not beg like a coward.

sentences.zh: 明公將以大義平天下，豈可使秦無守信之臣乎！

translations.literal: The enlightened lord will use great righteousness to pacify the realm—how can you make Qin lack a faithful subject!"
translations.idiomatic: You claim to conquer by virtue—do not kill the one Qin man who keeps faith!"

sentences.zh: 」裕嘉而免之。

translations.literal: Yu praised him and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu admired him and let him live.

sentences.zh: 泓遣給事黃門侍郎姚和都屯于堯柳，以備田子。

translations.literal: Hong sent attendant gentleman Huangmen Yao Hedou to camp at Yaoliu to prepare for Tianzi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong posted Yao Hedou at Yaoliu against Shen Tianzi.

sentences.zh: 姚紹謂諸將曰：「道濟等遠來送死，眾旅不多，嬰壘自固者，正欲曠日持久，以待繼援耳。

translations.literal: Yao Shao said to the generals, "Daoji and others have come from afar to deliver death; their hosts are not many; hugging ramparts and self-fortifying—they only wish to prolong days and months to await follow-up relief.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao told his generals: "Jin hugs its walls waiting for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 吾欲分軍還據閿鄉，以絕其糧運，不至一月，道濟之首可懸之麾下矣。

translations.literal: I wish to divide the army and return to hold Wenxiang to cut their grain transport—within not one month, Daoji's head can hang beneath the banner.
translations.idiomatic: Send a column to Wenxiang to sever their supplies and Tan Daoji's head will be on your pole within a month.

sentences.zh: 濟等既沒，裕計自沮。

translations.literal: Once Ji and others are gone, Yu's plan will naturally be blocked."
translations.idiomatic: Kill Tan Daoji and Liu Yu loses his spear point."

sentences.zh: 」諸將咸以為然。

translations.literal: All generals all thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: The generals agreed.

sentences.zh: 其將胡翼度曰：「軍勢宜集不可以分，若偏師不利，人心駭懼，胡可以戰！

translations.literal: His general Hu Yidu said, "Army momentum ought to be gathered and cannot be divided; if a partial army is not successful, human hearts will be terrified with alarm—how then can we fight!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yidu objected: "Split the army and one defeat routs every heart—you cannot fight divided."

sentences.zh: 」紹乃止。

translations.literal: Closing quotation: Shao then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao dropped his plan to split the army.

sentences.zh: 薛帛據河曲以叛。

translations.literal: Xue Bo occupied the river bend in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bo rebelled from the river bend.

sentences.zh: 紹分道置諸軍為掎角之勢，遣輔國胡翼度據東原，武衛姚鸞營于大路，與晉軍相接。

translations.literal: Shao divided roads and set various armies in horn-and-flank posture, sent General Who Supports the State Hu Yidu to hold the eastern plain, Martial Guard Yao Luan to camp on the great road, connecting with the Jin army.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao spread his wings: Hu Yidu on the east plain, Yao Luan on the main road, pressing Jin.

sentences.zh: 沈林子簡精銳銜枚夜襲之，鸞眾潰戰死，士卒死者九千餘人。

translations.literal: Shen Linzi picked crack troops, held mouthpieces for a night raid; Luan's host broke in battle and died; more than nine thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linzi night-attacked; Yao Luan fell with nine thousand men.

sentences.zh: 姚贊屯於河上，遣恢武姚難運蒲阪穀以給其軍，至香城，為王師所敗。

translations.literal: Yao Zan camped on the river, sent General Who Restores Might Yao Nan to transport Puban grain to supply the army; reaching Xiangcheng, he was defeated by the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan tried to ship grain from Puban but Jin smashed the train at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 時泓遣姚諶守堯柳，姚和都討薛帛於河東，聞王師要難，乃兼道赴救，未至而難敗，固破裕裨將于河曲，遂屯蒲阪。

translations.literal: At the time Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu, Yao Hedou campaigned against Xue Bo in Hedong; hearing the royal army was intercepting Nan, they hurried by combined roads to rescue; before arriving Nan was defeated, yet they broke Liu Yu's lieutenant at the river bend, then camped at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chen raced to save Yao Nan, missed him, but beat a Jin column in the bend and held Puban.

sentences.zh: 姚贊為林子所敗，單馬奔定城。

translations.literal: Yao Zan was defeated by Linzi, alone on horseback fled to Dingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan fled alone to Dingcheng after Shen Linzi routed him.

sentences.zh: 紹遣左長史姚洽及姚墨蠡等率騎三千屯于河北之九原，欲絕道濟諸縣租輸。

translations.literal: Shao sent left chief clerk Yao Qia and Yao Moli and others leading three thousand horse to camp at Jiuyuan north of the He, wishing to cut off Daoji's county rent convoys.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao sent Yao Qia to Jiuyuan to choke Tan Daoji's supply convoys.

sentences.zh: 洽辭曰：「夫小敵之堅，大敵之擒。

translations.literal: Qia declined, saying, "The firmness of a small enemy is the great enemy's catch.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Qia refused: "A small force that stands stubborn becomes bait.

sentences.zh: 今兵眾單弱，而遠在河外，雖明公神武，然鞭短勢殊，恐無所及。

translations.literal: Now the troops are few and weak and far beyond the river—though the enlightened lord is divinely martial, yet the whip is short and the power situation unequal—I fear there is no reaching them."
translations.idiomatic: We are too few and too far—even you cannot stretch a whip across the river."

sentences.zh: 」紹不聽。

translations.literal: Shao did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao ignored him.

sentences.zh: 沈林子率眾八千，耍洽於河上，洽戰死，眾皆沒。

translations.literal: Shen Linzi led eight thousand hosts, intercepted Qia on the river; Qia died in battle, the host all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linzi destroyed Yao Qia on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 紹聞洽等敗，忿恚發病，托姚贊以後事，使姚難屯關西，紹嘔血而死。

translations.literal: When Shao heard Qia and others were defeated, anger and vexation brought illness; he entrusted later affairs to Yao Zan, sent Yao Nan to camp west of the pass; Shao vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao died of rage and bleeding after Yao Qia's loss.

sentences.zh: 泓以晉師之逼，遣使乞師于魏。

translations.literal: Because the Jin army pressed, Hong sent envoys begging troops from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong begged Northern Wei for aid against Jin.

sentences.zh: 魏遣司徒、南平公拔拔嵩，正直將軍、安平公乙旃眷，進據河內，遊擊將軍王洛生屯於河東，為泓聲援。

translations.literal: Wei sent Minister of Education Duke of Nanping Baba Song, straight general Duke of Pingyi Yizhan Juan, and raiding general Wang Luosheng to camp in Hedong as sounding support for Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Baba Song and others to threaten Liu Yu's flank.

sentences.zh: 劉裕次於陝城，遣沈林子率精兵萬餘，越山開道，會沈田子等於青泥，將攻堯柳。

translations.literal: Liu Yu halted at Shan city, sent Shen Linzi with more than ten thousand crack troops to cross mountains opening roads, join Shen Tianzi and others at Qingni, planning to attack Yaoliu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Shen Linzi overland to Qingni against Yaoliu.

sentences.zh: 泓使姚裕率步騎八千距之，泓躬將大眾繼發。

translations.literal: Hong sent Yao Yu with eight thousand foot and horse to block them; Hong personally led the great host to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong marched with Yao Yu to meet them.

sentences.zh: 裕為田子所敗，泓退次於灞上，關中郡縣多潛通于王師。

translations.literal: Yu was defeated by Tianzi; Hong drew back to camp at Bashang; many Guanzhong counties secretly communicated with the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yu lost to Shen Tianzi; Yao Hong fell back to Bashang as towns went over to Jin.

sentences.zh: 劉裕至潼關，遣將軍硃超石、徐猗之會薛帛于河北，以攻蒲阪。

translations.literal: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass, sent generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yi to join Xue Bo north of the He to attack Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Zhu Chaoshi to strike Puban from the north bank.

sentences.zh: 姚贊距裕于關西，姚難屯於香城。

translations.literal: Yao Zan blocked Yu west of the pass; Yao Nan camped at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan faced Liu Yu; Yao Nan held Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 裕遣王鎮惡、王敬自秋社西渡渭，以逼難軍。

translations.literal: Yu sent Wang Zhen'e and Wang Chong west from Qiushe to cross the Wei, pressing Nan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e crossed the Wei against Yao Nan.

sentences.zh: 鎮東姚璞及姚和都擊敗猗之等於蒲阪，猗之遇害，超石棄其眾奔於潼關。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the East Yao Pu and Yao Hedou defeated Yi and others at Puban; Yi met death; Chaoshi abandoned his host and fled to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Pu crushed Jin at Puban; Xu Yi died and Zhu Chaoshi ran.

sentences.zh: 姚贊遣司馬休之及司馬國璠自軹關向河內，引魏軍以躡裕後。

translations.literal: Yao Zan sent Sima Xiuzhi and Simo Guofan from Zhiguan toward Hedong, drawing Wei troops to tread on Yu's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan tried to bring Wei in against Liu Yu's rear.

sentences.zh: 姚難既為鎮惡所逼，引師而西。

translations.literal: Nan, already pressed by Zhen'e, drew the army westward.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Nan retreated west before Wang Zhen'e.

sentences.zh: 時大霖雨，渭水泛溢，贊等不得北渡。

translations.literal: At the time great rains fell in succession, the Wei overflowed; Zan and others could not cross north.
translations.idiomatic: Floods blocked Yao Zan from crossing the Wei.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡水陸兼進，追及姚難。

translations.literal: Zhen'e advanced by water and land together, caught up with Yao Nan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e overtook Yao Nan in the flood season.

sentences.zh: 泓自灞上還軍，次於石橋以援之。

translations.literal: Hong returned the army from Bashang, halted at Stone Bridge to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong rushed to Stone Bridge to help.

sentences.zh: 贊退屯鄭城。

translations.literal: Zan drew back to camp at Zheng city.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan fell back to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 鎮北姚彊率郡人數千，與姚難陣於涇上，以距鎮惡。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North Yao Qiang led several thousand commandery people and with Yao Nan formed array on the Jing to block Zhen'e.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Qiang joined Yao Nan on the Jing River line.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡遣毛德祖擊彊，大敗，彊戰死，難遁還長安。

translations.literal: Zhen'e sent Mao Dezu to strike Qiang, greatly defeated him; Qiang died in battle; Nan fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dezu killed Yao Qiang; Yao Nan bolted for Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 劉裕進據鄭城。

translations.literal: Liu Yu advanced and occupied Zheng city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu took Zheng.

sentences.zh: 泓使姚裕、尚書龐統屯兵宮中，姚洸屯於灃西，尚書姚白瓜徙四軍雜戶入長安，姚丕守渭橋，胡翼度屯石積，姚贊屯霸東，泓軍於逍遙園。

translations.literal: Hong sent Yao Yu and Minister Pang Tong to camp troops in the palace, Yao Guang west of the Feng, Minister Yao Baigua moved four-army miscellaneous households into Chang'an, Yao Pi guarded Wei Bridge, Hu Yidu camped at Stone Accumulation, Yao Zan east of Ba; Hong encamped at Free-Roam Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong strung his last line from the palace to the Wei bridge and Free-Roam Garden.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡夾渭進兵，破姚丕於渭橋。

translations.literal: Zhen'e advanced troops on both sides of the Wei, defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e shattered Yao Pi at the Wei bridge.

sentences.zh: 泓自逍遙園赴之，逼水地狹，因丕之敗，遂相踐而退。

translations.literal: Hong went from Free-Roam Garden to aid him; pressed by water, ground narrow, because of Pi's defeat, they trampled each other in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong's relief column stampeded itself in the narrow river flats.

sentences.zh: 姚諶及前軍姚烈、左衛姚寶安、散騎王帛、建武姚進、揚威姚蠔、尚書右丞孫玄等皆死於陣，泓單馬還宮。

translations.literal: Yao Chen and forward army Yao Lie, left guard Yao Bao'an, supernumerary Wang Bo, Jianwei Yao Jin, General Who Displays Might Yao Hao, right aide Sun Xuan and others all died in formation; Hong alone on horseback returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong's generals died to a man; he galloped alone back into the palace.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡入自平朔門，泓與姚裕等數百騎出奔于石橋。

translations.literal: Zhen'e entered from Pingshuo Gate; Hong with Yao Yu and several hundred horse fled out toward Stone Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e broke Pingshuo Gate; Yao Hong fled toward Stone Bridge.

sentences.zh: 贊聞泓之敗也，召將士告之，眾皆以刀擊地，攘袂大泣。

translations.literal: When Zan heard of Hong's defeat, he summoned officers and soldiers and told them; all struck the earth with knives, pulled sleeves and wept greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan's men wept and beat the ground when they heard the news.

sentences.zh: 胡翼度先與劉裕陰通，是日棄眾奔裕。

translations.literal: Hu Yidu had earlier secretly communicated with Liu Yu; that day he abandoned the host and fled to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yidu defected to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 贊夜率諸軍，將會泓于石橋，王師已固諸門，贊軍不得入，眾皆驚散。

translations.literal: Zan by night led all armies, planning to join Hong at Stone Bridge; the royal army had already secured all gates; Zan's army could not enter; the host all startled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan could not re-enter the sealed capital.

sentences.zh: 泓計無所出，謀欲降於裕。

translations.literal: Hong had no plan left, plotted wishing to surrender to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong decided to surrender to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 其子佛念，年十一，謂泓曰：「晉人將逞其欲，終必不全，願自裁決。

translations.literal: His son Fonian, age eleven, said to Hong, "The Jin people will indulge their desires to the end—you will surely not be preserved whole; I wish to decide for myself."
translations.idiomatic: His eleven-year-old son Yao Fonian said: "Surrender will not save us—better to die cleanly."

sentences.zh: 」泓憮然不答。

translations.literal: Hong looked mournful and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong could not answer.

sentences.zh: 佛念遂登宮牆自投而死。

translations.literal: Fonian then climbed the palace wall and threw himself down to die.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Fonian leaped from the palace wall.

sentences.zh: 泓將妻子詣壘門而降。

translations.literal: Hong led wife and children to the camp gate and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong brought his family to Liu Yu's camp and yielded.

sentences.zh: 贊率宗室子弟百餘人亦降於裕，裕盡殺之，余宗遷於江南。

translations.literal: Zan led more than a hundred sons and nephews of the imperial clan also to surrender to Yu; Yu killed them all; the rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu slaughtered the surrendered Yao princes and deported the clan to the south.

sentences.zh: 送泓于建康市斬之，時年三十，在位二年。

translations.literal: They sent Hong to Jiankang market and beheaded him; he was thirty years old, on the throne two years.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong was executed in the Jiankang market at thirty after two years' reign.

sentences.zh: 建康百里之內，草木皆燋死焉。

translations.literal: Within a hundred li of Jiankang, grass and trees all scorched dead.
translations.idiomatic: Grass and trees withered for a hundred li around Jiankang—omen of the tyrant's fall.

sentences.zh: 姚萇以孝武僭立，至泓三世，以安帝而滅，凡三十二年。

translations.literal: Yao Chang presumptuously rose under Emperor Xiaowu; down to Hong three generations; with Emperor An they perished—thirty-two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Yao Chang's usurpation to Yao Hong's death the Later Qin lasted three reigns and thirty-two years under Jin's An era.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Rubric title: Historical Appraisal (史評).
translations.idiomatic: Section heading marking a later historical appraisal.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自長江徙禦，化龍創業，巨寇乘機而未寧，戎馬交馳而不息，晦重氛於六漠，鼓洪流於八際，天未厭亂，凶旅實繁。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: From moving the defense to the Yangtze, transforming dragon and founding enterprise, great bandits seized the chance and were not yet quiet; war-horses galloped one upon another without rest; heavy murk veiled the six deserts, great floods drummed the eight bounds—Heaven had not tired of chaos, and fierce hosts were truly many.
translations.idiomatic: The historian opens: age of warlords and tribal armies without end.

sentences.zh: 弋仲越自金方，言歸石氏，抗直詞於暴主，闡忠訓于危朝，貽厥之謀，在乎歸順，鳴哀之義，有足稱焉。

translations.literal: Yizhong crossed from the metal quarter, spoke of returning to the Shi house, raised straight words to a violent lord, spread loyal instruction in a perilous court—his plan for posterity lay in submission; the meaning of his lament is worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong defied Shi Hu yet sought peace—his loyalty earns praise.

sentences.zh: 景國弱歲英奇，見方孫策，詳其幹識，無忝斯言，遂踐迷途，良可悲矣！

translations.literal: Jingguo in weak years was heroic and strange, compared to Sun Ce; examining his capacity and insight, he did not shame that saying—yet he trod a lost road, truly lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang matched Sun Ce in dash but marched into tragedy.

sentences.zh: 景茂因仲襄之緒，躡苻亡之會，嘯命群豪，恢弘霸業，假容沖之銳，俯定函、秦；

translations.literal: Jingmao took up Zhongxiang's thread, stepped into Fu's fall, whistled command to the heroes, enlarged the hegemon's enterprise—borrowed Chong's edge to bow and settle Han and Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang used Yao Xiang's legacy to seize Chang'an when Fu Jian fell.

sentences.zh: 挫雷惡之鋒，載甯東北。

translations.literal: broke the point of Lei E, brought peace to the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: He broke Murong Chui's power and quieted the northeast.

sentences.zh: 在茲奸略，實冠凶徒。

translations.literal: In these crafty stratagems he truly crowned the villains.
translations.idiomatic: In cunning he outdid every rival warlord.

sentences.zh: 列樹而表新營，雖云效績；

translations.literal: Planting trees to mark new camps—though called achievement;
translations.idiomatic: He marked new camps with trees—passing as order.

sentences.zh: 薦棘而陵舊主，何其不仁！

translations.literal: pushing brambles to climb the old lord—how lacking in benevolence!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he trampled his old lord Fu Jian—heartless.

sentences.zh: 安枕而終，斯為幸也。

translations.literal: To pillow in peace and end—this was fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He died in bed—that was luck enough.

sentences.zh: 子略克摧勍敵，荷成先構，虛襟訪道，側席求賢，敦友弟以睦其親，明賞罰以臨其下，英髦盡節，爪牙畢命。

translations.literal: Zilue was able to crush mighty foes, bore the completed prior structure, emptied breast to visit the Way, set aside mat to seek worthies, thickly befriended younger brothers to harmonize kin, clarified rewards and punishments to face those below—heroes exhausted their integrity, claws and fangs gave their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing broke strong enemies, finished his father's work, sought wise counsel, knit his clan, and ruled with clear rewards—rivaling Zhuang of Chu or Mu of Qin.

sentences.zh: 取汾、絳，陷許、洛，款僭燕而籓偽蜀，夷隴右而靜河西，俗阜年豐，遠安邇輯，雖楚莊、秦穆何以加焉！

translations.literal: He took Fen and Jiang, fell Xu and Luo, treated false Yan as vassal and hedged false Shu, leveled Longyou and quieted Hexi—customs rich, years abundant, far quieted and near gathered—though Chu Zhuang or Qin Mu, how could they surpass!
translations.idiomatic: At his height he held the heartland and the west in prosperity few could match.

sentences.zh: 既而逞志矜功，弗虞後患。

translations.literal: Yet afterward he indulged his will and boasted of merit, did not guard against later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Then pride undid his caution.

sentences.zh: 委涼都於禿髮，授朔方於赫連，專己生災，邊城繼陷，距諫招禍，蕭牆屢發，戰無寧歲，人有危心。

translations.literal: He entrusted Liangzhou to Tufa, handed Shuofang to Helian, trusting himself bred disaster; border cities fell in succession, rejecting remonstrance invited calamity; inner walls rose again and again; war without quiet years, men harbored peril in heart.
translations.idiomatic: He gave the west to Tufa Lianggu and the north to Helian Bobo, ignored advice, and border disaster followed year on year.

sentences.zh: 豈宜騁彼雄圖，被深恩於介士；

translations.literal: How fitting to ride those heroic plans and spread deep favor on armored men—
translations.idiomatic: He should have showered his soldiers with thanks—

sentences.zh: 翻崇詭說，加殊禮于桑門！

translations.literal: yet he reversed course to honor crafty doctrine and piled special rites on shaven monks!
translations.idiomatic: —yet he lavished gold on Buddhist monks instead.

sentences.zh: 當有為之時，肄無為之業，麗衣腴食，殆將萬數，析實談空，靡然成俗。

translations.literal: In a time when action was needed, he practiced non-action's enterprise; gorgeous robes and rich food approached ten thousand; splitting substance they talked emptiness—became custom on the wind.
translations.idiomatic: He let monasteries swell while taxes bled the hills.

sentences.zh: 夫以漢朝殷廣，猶鄙鴻都之費；

translations.literal: Even Han's vast abundance still despised Hongdu's expense;
translations.idiomatic: Even the vast Han court scorned the waste of the Hongdu academy.

sentences.zh: 況乎偽境日侵，寧堪永貴之役！

translations.literal: how much more when false borders daily shrank—could it bear eternal costly service!
translations.idiomatic: How much less could a shrinking rebel realm bear endless monastic extravagance?

sentences.zh: 儲用殫竭，山林有稅，政荒威挫，職是之由，坐致淪胥，非天喪也。

translations.literal: Stores were exhausted, hills and forests taxed; government wild, awe broken—this is the reason; sitting to bring ruin—Heaven did not destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Empty treasuries and forest levies—not fate but policy destroyed Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 元子以庸懦之質，屬傾擾之餘，內難方殷，外禦斯輟。

translations.literal: Yuanzi with a mediocre and timid substance, amid the aftermath of overturn and turmoil, inner disaster just raging, outer defense then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong was weak when kin tore the realm apart and Jin struck.

sentences.zh: 王師杖順，弭節而下長安；

translations.literal: The royal army wielded obedience, lowered the pace and descended on Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: Jin marched in righteousness and took Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 凶嗣失圖，系組而降軹道。

translations.literal: the wicked heir lost his plan, tied cord and surrendered at Zhidao.
translations.idiomatic: the last heir bound himself at Zhidao.

sentences.zh: 物極則反，抑斯之謂歟！

translations.literal: Things extreme then reverse—does this say it!
translations.idiomatic: Thus the wheel turns: extremes invite reversal.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：弋仲剛烈，終表奇節。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: Yizhong was stern and fierce, in the end displayed a strange integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Yao Yizhong died unbroken.

sentences.zh: 襄實英果，萇惟奸傑。

translations.literal: Xiang was truly heroic and resolute; Chang alone was a treacherous champion.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang was bold; Yao Chang was the cunning founder.

sentences.zh: 興始崇構，泓遂摧滅。

translations.literal: Xing first raised the frame; Hong then was destroyed and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing built the state; Yao Hong watched it fall.

sentences.zh: 貽誡將來，無踐危轍。

translations.literal: Leave warning to those who come—do not tread this perilous rut.
translations.idiomatic: Let later ages shun that fatal road.
